title: Underived proper exchange is an isomorphism
statement:
For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$
proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and every torsion etale sheaf
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, the map

$$
 \Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For a sheaf F and an algebraic-closure point s of Yprime, form the cartesian base change of fprime along s. The map fprime is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Both that square and its horizontal paste with the given square are geometric-point base changes of proper maps. Their exchange components are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-geometric-point-exchange].

proof.text: Use the underived horizontal pasting identity [lem-weil-pbc-underived-horizontal-pasting], implemented by Etale.baseChangeMap_paste_horiz_app. The exchange of the outer square is the composite of the upperStar composition isomorphism, s inverse image of the original exchange, the exchange of the second square, and a direct image of the inverse upperStar composition isomorphism. Cancel the three isomorphisms to conclude that s inverse image of the original exchange component is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The natural stalk-pullback comparison of [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], implemented by upperStarCompSheafFiberIso at the identity geometric point of Spec Omega, identifies the original stalk map with the fibre of s inverse image of that component. A functor preserves isomorphisms; transport across this natural comparison and the universe-lift fibre isomorphism. All algebraic-closure stalks of the original component are isomorphisms, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes it an isomorphism. NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app then makes the exchange natural transformation an isomorphism.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
If $f$ is proper, then
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$ is an
isomorphism for every sheaf $F$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Fix a geometric point $\bar y'\to Y'$ and let $\bar y\to Y$ be its composite
with $g$. Let $\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the category of
pointed affine etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$. It is
cofiltered: an affine open containing the lifted point in a fibre product
refines two objects, and an affine neighbourhood of the equalizer of two
maps makes parallel maps equal. It is cofinal among all pointed etale
neighbourhoods because every lifted point has an affine open neighbourhood.
Thus

$$
(f_*F)_{\bar y}=
\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)}\Gamma(X\times_YV,F|).
$$

Writing $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, the strict henselization is
$Y_{(\bar y)}=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim A_V)$ and
$X_{(\bar y)}=X\times_YY_{(\bar y)}=\varprojlim(X\times_YV)$. The natural
map from the displayed colimit to $\Gamma(X_{(\bar y)},F|)$ is bijective.
For surjectivity, represent a section on the limit by sections on a finite
cover by quasi-compact etale objects. Each object, each covering map, and
each section representative descends to a stage because etale morphisms are
locally of finite presentation. The finitely many equality conditions on
the pairwise fibre products descend after enlarging that stage. The sheaf
equalizer then glues the descended representatives. For injectivity,
represent two sections at one stage; equality on the limit is witnessed on
a finite etale cover, and the cover together with its finitely many equality
witnesses descends to a later stage. Hence the two representatives agree in
the colimit.

The base $Y_{(\bar y)}$ is strictly henselian local and
$X_{(\bar y)}$ is proper over it. The preceding lemma identifies its
sections with those on the closed geometric fibre:

$$
(f_*F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Gamma(X_{(\bar y)},F|)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Gamma(X_{\bar y},F|_{X_{\bar y}}).
$$

The identical construction for $f'$ gives the target stalk. Since $\bar y$
is the composite of the same $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$ with $g$,
the Cartesian isomorphism identifies $X_{\bar y}$ and $X'_{\bar y'}$ with
$X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.

Finally, a germ represented by $s\in\Gamma(X\times_YV,F|)$ travels around
the comparison by pulling $s$ first to $X'\times_{Y'}(V\times_YY')$ and then
to the geometric fibre. The two stalk identifications above pull $s$
directly to that same fibre. Hence the fibre bijection is the stalk of
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$, not an unnamed isomorphism. Geometric
stalks are conservative, so the exchange map is an isomorphism. This closes
the compatibility omission at Tag `0A3U`.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. For a cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f$ proper
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and every etale sheaf $F$ of
$\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ (in particular every etale abelian sheaf
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]), the map

$$
 \Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism. Moreover, for an
abelian sheaf $F$ and a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$
with geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the map

$$
 (f_*F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_{\bar y},F|_{X_{\bar y}}),
$$

sending a germ represented by a section of $F$ over $X\times_YV$ to its
restriction to the fibre, is bijective.

proof.text:
Whether $\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism only depends on the underlying
abelian sheaves, so let $F$ be abelian.

*The stalk formula.* Let $\bar y\to Y$ be a geometric point and let
$\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the category of pointed affine etale
neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$; it is cofiltered and cofinal among all
pointed etale neighbourhoods [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal].
Thus

$$
(f_*F)_{\bar y}=
\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)}\Gamma(X\times_YV,F|).
$$

Writing $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, the strict localization is
$Y_{(\bar y)}=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim A_V)$
[def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and
$X_{(\bar y)}=X\times_YY_{(\bar y)}=\varprojlim(X\times_YV)$. The natural
map from the displayed colimit to $\Gamma(X_{(\bar y)},F|)$ is bijective.
For surjectivity, represent a section on the limit by sections on a finite
cover by quasi-compact etale objects. Each object, each covering map, and
each section representative descends to a stage because etale morphisms are
locally of finite presentation. The finitely many equality conditions on
the pairwise fibre products descend after enlarging that stage. The sheaf
equalizer then glues the descended representatives. For injectivity,
represent two sections at one stage; equality on the limit is witnessed on
a finite etale cover, and the cover together with its finitely many equality
witnesses descends to a later stage. Hence the two representatives agree in
the colimit.

The local ring of $Y_{(\bar y)}$ is strictly henselian and $X_{(\bar y)}$ is
proper over it, so [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-strict-henselian-h0] identifies
$\Gamma(X_{(\bar y)},F|)$ with the sections over the closed geometric fibre
$X\times_Y\Spec\kappa^{\mathrm{alg}}$, $\kappa^{\mathrm{alg}}\subseteq\Omega$ the
algebraic closure of the residue field of $Y_{(\bar y)}$. Sections of the
pullback of an etale sheaf do not change under an extension
$\kappa^{\mathrm{alg}}\subseteq\Omega$ of algebraically closed ground fields
(Stacks Project, Tag 0A3I), so

$$
(f_*F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Gamma(X_{(\bar y)},F|)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Gamma(X_{\bar y},F|_{X_{\bar y}}),
$$

and the composite is the restriction map of the statement.

*The exchange map.* Fix a geometric point $\bar y'\to Y'$ and let $\bar y\to Y$
be its composite with $g$. Properness is stable under base change, so the stalk
formula applies to $f'$ as well. The cartesian square identifies $X_{\bar y}$ and
$X'_{\bar y'}$ with $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and the two inverse
images of $F$ on it. A germ represented by $s\in\Gamma(X\times_YV,F|)$ is sent by
$\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ to the germ of its pullback to $X'\times_{Y'}(V\times_YY')$
(the description of the underived exchange on sections, natural in $F$
[lemma-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-naturality]), and both stalk identifications
then restrict $s$ to the same fibre. Hence the induced map of stalks is the
identity under these identifications. Geometric stalks are conservative
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], so $\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ is an
isomorphism.
